data.title: Newer antileprosy drugs (ofloxacin, moxifloxacin, minocycline, clarithromycin, rifapentine, ethionamide)
data.summary: Antileprosy drugs · Second-line bactericidal drugs used for resistance, intolerance and alternative regimens
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antileprosy drugs_

**Class:** Second-line bactericidal drugs used for resistance, intolerance and alternative regimens

## Mechanism of action
- Fluoroquinolones (ofloxacin, moxifloxacin): inhibit DNA gyrase — strongly bactericidal against M. leprae (moxifloxacin is the most potent)
- Minocycline: 30S ribosome inhibitor; the only tetracycline with significant activity against M. leprae
- Clarithromycin: 50S ribosome inhibitor; bactericidal against M. leprae
- Rifapentine: long-acting rifamycin, more potent than rifampicin in mice
- Ethionamide/prothionamide: inhibit mycolic acid synthesis; hepatotoxic — rarely used now

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Rifampicin-resistant leprosy (with clofazimine)
- Patients intolerant of standard MDT drugs
- ROM regimens and trial regimens (e.g. rifapentine–moxifloxacin–minocycline, PEP studies)

## Dose & formulations
- Ofloxacin 400 mg daily; moxifloxacin 400 mg daily; minocycline 100 mg daily; clarithromycin 500 mg daily
- Rifapentine 900 mg monthly (in trial regimens)

## Adverse effects
- Fluoroquinolones: GI upset, tendinopathy, QT prolongation, CNS effects, photosensitivity (sparfloxacin)
- Minocycline: vestibular effects, pigmentation, autoimmune reactions
- Clarithromycin: GI upset, taste change, CYP3A4 interactions
- Ethionamide: severe hepatotoxicity, GI upset

## Contraindications
- Fluoroquinolones in pregnancy and children (cartilage effects — relative)
- Minocycline in pregnancy and children under 8

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid fluoroquinolones and minocycline in pregnancy; clarithromycin with caution.

## Viva points
- Most bactericidal second-line drugs: moxifloxacin, rifapentine
- ROM = rifampicin + ofloxacin + minocycline
- Rifampicin-resistant leprosy = clofazimine + 2 of (FQ, minocycline, clarithromycin)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.6 (Newer drugs in leprosy); Wolverton 4e ch.9; WHO 2018 leprosy guidelines. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
